sections.title: What Your Love Language Reveals About You

items.q: What should you remember about **Not just romance**?
items.a: **love languages apply to children, friends,** parents, and colleagues; physical touch includes hugs, shoulder pats, sitting close in non-romantic contexts.

items.q: What should you remember about **Hurt-test for self-diagnosis**?
items.a: **fastest sting reveals primary language**: ignored entry, no time together, no help offered, forgotten gift occasions, or physical distance.

items.q: What should you remember about **Both can love and still miss**?
items.a: **Vinh poured words; wife showed acts** of service; neither felt loved until they translated into the other's language.

items.q: What should you remember about **Practicing foreign languages feels weird**?
items.a: **gift-givers may feel shallow; touch-averse people** may resist hugs; don't judge others' languages; do it for them, not you.

items.q: What should you remember about **Covert vs overt identification**?
items.a: **observe what would hurt them** most (approximate) or send this video and ask directly (accurate).

items.q: What should you remember about **Visible reminders**?
items.a: **write each person's language somewhere you see daily;** 10+ years in, Vinh still needs the cue because defaulting to your own language is a hard habit.

items.q: What should you remember about **Per-language playbook**?
items.a: **words**: sni framework regularly; quality time: phone away, undivided attention; acts of service: 1–3 daily tasks, never bail; physical touch: small consistent contact; gifts: thoughtful tokens, not expensive splurges.
